source_level_claims_to_prove.label: l:presieving
source_level_claims_to_prove.title: Two-range presieving deduction
source_level_claims_to_prove.statement_latex:
\label{l:presieving}
Suppose that
\begin{align}\label{e:circestsieve}
 |\mathcal F_d|=Xg(d)+r_d,
\end{align}
where \(g\) is multiplicative on the square-free integers supported on
a fixed set of primes \(\mathfrak P\), and \(0\leq g(p)<1\).  Let
\(2\leq R<z\), and suppose that there are fixed constants
\(\kappa_0,\kappa,K_0>0\) such that
\begin{align}\label{e:tworangesievedimension}
 \prod_{\substack{w\leq p<y\\p\in\mathfrak P}}
 \left(1-g(p)\right)^{-1}
 &\leq
 K_0\left(\frac{\log y}{\log w}\right)^{\kappa_0},
 &&2\leq w<y\leq R,\notag\\
 \prod_{\substack{w\leq p<y\\p\in\mathfrak P}}
 \left(1-g(p)\right)^{-1}
 &\leq
 K_0\left(\frac{\log y}{\log w}\right)^\kappa,
 &&R<w<y\leq z.
\end{align}
Define 
\[
 D_0=\exp((\log\log N)^3),\qquad D_1=D/D_0, \qquad D_0<D , \qquad \frac{\log D_0}{\log R}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Then
\begin{align}\label{e:presievedbounds10}
 S(\mathcal F,\mathfrak P,z)
 &\geq XV(z)\bigl(f_\kappa(s)+o(1)\bigr)
 +\sum_{m<D}c_m^-r_m,\notag\\
 S(\mathcal F,\mathfrak P,z)
 &\leq XV(z)\bigl(F_\kappa(s)+o(1)\bigr)
 +\sum_{m<D}c_m^+r_m,
\end{align}
where
\[
 V(z)=\prod_{\substack{p<z\\p\in\mathfrak P}}(1-g(p)),
 \qquad
 s=\frac{\log D_1}{\log z},
 \qquad
 |c_m^\pm|\leq1.
\]
The coefficients \(c_m^\pm\) depend only on the fixed prime sets and
the sieve levels, and not on the values of \(g\).  
The dimension
\(\kappa_0\) is used only in the preliminary sieve over \(p\leq R\);
the sieve functions in \eqref{e:presievedbounds10} are determined by
the outer dimension \(\kappa\).

source_level_claims_to_prove.label: l:wumatomakisum
source_level_claims_to_prove.title: Weighted-prime sum in the upper sieve main term
source_level_claims_to_prove.statement_latex:
\label{l:wumatomakisum}
Let \(\alpha=9/8\).  Uniformly in the range \eqref{e:nrange10},
\begin{align}\label{e:wumatomakisum10}
 \sum_{\ell\in L}X_n(\ell)\Theta_{n,\ell}(z_\ell)
 \leq
 \bigl(c_\alpha\mathcal W(\alpha)+o(1)\bigr)
 X_n\Theta_n(z),
 \qquad
 c_\alpha=\frac{16e^{-\gamma/2}}{\sqrt{\pi\alpha}}.
\end{align}
Here \(\mathcal W(\alpha)\) is the integral defined in
\eqref{e:Wdef8}.
